summary: The Good Energy Jobs Act of 2026 amends the Department of Energy Organization Act to require recipients of Department of Energy financial assistance to meet specific labor standards, community benefit requirements, domestic manufacturing commitments, and provisions targeting small or disadvantaged communities.

affected_groups.effect: Must adhere to prevailing wage requirements, apprenticeship utilization quotas, labor neutrality certifications, and community benefits plans, with noncompliance risking financial assistance withholding or termination.
affected_groups.group: Contractors and subcontractors receiving Department of Energy financial assistance

affected_groups.effect: Guaranteed prevailing wages, increased access to registered apprenticeship programs, and protections related to union organizing and collective bargaining.
affected_groups.group: Laborers and mechanics on Department-assisted projects

affected_groups.effect: Targeted to receive at least 40 percent of financial assistance through specified programs, supported by mandatory community benefits plans and community needs assessments.

key_provisions: Requires contractors and subcontractors on Department-assisted projects to pay prevailing wages to laborers and mechanics.
Mandates that at least 15 percent of total labor hours on covered projects be performed by individuals in registered apprenticeship programs.
Requires financial assistance recipients and contractors to make a good-faith certification of labor neutrality regarding employees' rights to organize and bargain collectively.
Mandates project labor agreements for construction, alteration, maintenance, or repair of Department facilities costing more than $1,000,000.
Requires entities applying for financial assistance for covered projects to include a community benefits plan informed by a community needs assessment.

Directs the Secretary of Energy to promote domestic manufacturing and requires entities receiving research, development, or demonstration assistance to commit to manufacturing products substantially in the United States and submit a domestic manufacturing plan.
Establishes an initiative seeking to ensure that at least 40 percent of financial assistance through specified programs is provided to entities benefiting small or disadvantaged communities.
missing_information: Specific details on the exact definitions of prevailing wage rates in every locality prior to Secretary of Labor determinations.
The complete list of covered programs for the 40 percent small and disadvantaged communities initiative, which the Secretary is directed to issue within one year of enactment.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Good Energy Jobs Act of 2026 amends the Department of Energy Organization Act to require recipients of Department of Energy financial assistance to meet specific labor standards, community benefit requirements, domestic manufacturing commitments, and provisions targeting small or disadvantaged communities.
summary_detail.significance: This bill establishes a comprehensive set of federal mandates linking Department of Energy financial assistance directly to labor standards, domestic production requirements, and community benefit agreements, affecting all future grants, loans, loan guarantees, cooperative agreements, and prize competitions administered by the Department.

title: Good Energy Jobs Act of 2026
